assessment.rationale: No validated model explains how every human decision is made, so the Main KPI of 1 complete decision model is unmet. The strongest predictive candidate, Centaur (Nature 2025), was fine-tuned on Psych-101, about 10 million choices from 60,000 people in 160 experiments, and predicts held-out behaviour well (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40604288/); critics found it keeps choosing original-dataset answers under altered instructions, consistent with overfitting rather than a model of cognition (https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1116367, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.03311). Classic theories replicate only as tendencies: prospect theory patterns held in 19 countries with smaller effects and heterogeneity (https://research.vu.nl/en/publications/replicating-patterns-of-prospect-theory-for-decision-under-risk/). Neural mapping covers one mouse task: the International Brain Laboratory recorded 620,000 neurons across nearly the whole brain (https://pni.princeton.edu/news/2025/first-brain-wide-map-decision-making-charted-mice). Honest limit: complete is not testable as stated, data are mostly from Western samples, and Centaur and Psych-101 are open baselines, so retraining them is known work.

additionalSearches.finding: Prospect theory replicated in 4,098 people across 19 countries with smaller effects and notable heterogeneity; tendencies, not a complete model.

additionalSearches.query: Centaur criticism does not explain cognition out of distribution failures 2025
additionalSearches.finding: Zhejiang critique: under misleading or removed instructions Centaur still chose original answers, suggesting overfitting; other critiques say prediction is not explanation.

additionalSearches.query: neural basis of decision making complete model brain international brain laboratory brain-wide map decision 2025
additionalSearches.finding: IBL (Nature 2025) mapped 620,000 neurons in 139 mice for one visual decision task; decision signals are brain-wide; an integrated model is still future work.
